title: Penn World Table 10.01: the United States, 1950-2019
series: year; in the words of the sheet Legend: rgdpna ('Real GDP at constant 2017 national prices (in mil. 2017US$)'), emp ('Number of persons engaged (in millions)'), rnna ('Capital stock at constant 2017 national prices (in mil. 2017US$)'), labsh ('Share of labour compensation in GDP at current national prices'), pop ('Population (in millions)')
notes: Read from the workbook pwt1001.xlsx, sheet Data, downloaded from https://dataverse.nl/api/access/datafile/354095 (SHA-256 bf2b66c5fd8b465870eeab8bbfa3a57e73253a3236a933286259efbbb5fb67a2), whose SHA-1, 7461933f7561767ffbd77db3ab984d60cb21e9ef, is the one the dataset record gives. The figures are written as the workbook stores them (Python's repr of the float). The workbook's sheet Info says: 'When using these data, please refer to the following paper:' and gives the same reference. checks/check_ch40.py computes the growth of rgdpna/emp 1950-2019, the labour share of 1950 and 2019 and rnna/rgdpna in both years.
source: Penn World Table version 10.01, Groningen Growth and Development Centre, University of Groningen (DataverseNL, doi:10.34894/QT5BCC, released 2023-01-26)

Timmer (2015), "The Next Generation of the Penn World Table" American Economic Review, 105(10), 3150-3182, DOI: 10.1257/aer.20130954, available for download at www.ggdc.net/pwt'.
